vulnerability.category_l2: Exponential memory allocation through recursive collection-alias expansion (Billion Laughs) in the YAML parser

critical_operation.description: Parser::parseValue() handles a "*alias" value by looking the name up in $this->refs and returning the referenced value directly. At v5.4.45 the only guards are the missing-reference and circular-reference checks; the returned value may be an array or stdClass that itself contains aliases, so nested collection aliases expand multiplicatively at resolution time and a small untrusted document can allocate multi-gigabyte structures. The same unbounded return exists in the merge-key path (Parser.php line 256) and in Inline::evaluateScalar() (Inline.php line 594). The 5.4.52 fix routes all three paths through ParserState::countAlias(), which counts array/stdClass/TaggedValue resolutions and throws once the configurable limit (default 128) is exceeded; scalar aliases remain unrestricted.

entry_point.description: Yaml::parse() (or Parser::parse()) called on untrusted YAML containing anchors and "*alias" references to collections.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Parser::parseValue at v5.4.45 and confirm the alias lookup returns $this->refs[$value] with no count or size bound.
An independent reviewer must confirm the merge-key path and Inline::evaluateScalar have the same unbounded return.
An independent reviewer must confirm e77391b2 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the fix introduces ParserState::countAlias with a default limit of 128.
An independent reviewer must confirm ParserState.php is absent at v5.4.45 and that the prerequisite commit 914f427e is also absent from that tag.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP or YAML document was executed; the finding is static and the memory blow-up was not measured.
The 5.4 branch is the only one compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
At v5.4.45 there is no ParserState; the fix depends on 914f427e (recursion-depth bounding, CVE-2026-45133) which landed just before it, so the backport history is coupled.
The GHSA label LOW and OSV VA:L vector disagree materially with the CNA 8.7 and NVD 7.5 scores.
open_questions: Whether the merge-key path (line 256) alone is sufficient for exponential growth was not analysed beyond reading the code.
Whether the 5.4 fix also needs the 914f427e prerequisite to apply cleanly to arbitrary downstream patch sets was not assessed.
CWE-776 is defined for XML DTD entity expansion; all three primary sources apply it to YAML alias expansion, which is an upstream classification choice rather than a dossier error.
